resources.string: Showing charge level on the Glyph interface
Your phone lets this app use the Glyph interface. Nothing else to set up.
The app has permission to turn on Glyph debug mode itself and will keep doing so. Nothing else to set up.
Your phone blocks Glyph control for third-party apps by default. Connect it to a computer with USB debugging enabled and run the command below.

You run this command only once. After that the app turns on debug mode by itself, so you will not need to return to the computer. Debug mode resets every 48 hours, and this permission is what lets the app restore it.
Install Shizuku and start it on your phone using wireless debugging. Then allow this app below. Shizuku has to be started again after every reboot.
Shizuku is not running. Start it, then tap Check again.
Shizuku is running. Allow this app to use it.
Access was denied. Allow Glyph Meter in the Shizuku app, then tap Check again.
This app needs a Nothing phone with a Glyph interface. This device is not a Nothing phone or its model is not recognized.
The meter stays lit for as long as the phone is charging.
The meter appears when you plug in and after each step of charge, then fades.
Glyph access is managed by the app
Smoothness is reduced. Nothing removed per-segment brightness on this phone, so the meter moves in whole-segment steps.

The Glyph service refused this app. On Nothing OS 3.x this usually means Glyph debug mode has expired and the app has no permission to turn it back on. Open Details above for the one-time setup, then check again.
The Glyph service could not be reached or would not open a session. Check again in a moment; restarting the phone usually helps.
The system closed the connection to the Glyph and reconnecting did not work. Check again to retry.
The Glyph accepted the connection but could not draw the meter. Check again to retry.
The Glyph service is not available right now. Check again to retry.
Skip lighting the Glyph while the phone lies screen up.
